preamble: The voiced alveolar affricate [dz] (POJ j-) merges with the lateral [l] in Quanzhou-type Hokkien. Where Zhangzhou-type varieties keep the Southern Min voiced initial (which goes back mostly to Proto-Min nasal initials) as [dz] or [z], Quanzhou, Xiamen and the Taipei and Lukang accents of Taiwan pronounce it [l], so that 字, 二, 人 and 熱 begin with [l] in these varieties. The change is well documented but confined to Southern Min.

examples.note: Most Quanzhou dialects have no /dz/ initial, having merged it into /l/. The from forms show the conservative Southern Min /dz/ initial, which Quanzhou merged into /l/.
